# 1.2.63 - what only the GMs may know, kept by the GMs

The seventh stage on the way to 1.3.0. What only the GMs may know - the case -
no longer lives in one GM's browser: each GM's browser keeps a copy of it for
each world, the browsers exchange it field by field, and a backup file can
bring it back. The world is migrated on the first load, and nothing leaves the
world's data before the new store has read it back.

## Before installing

1. **Copy the world** (Foundry's backup of the world in Setup, or a copy of the
   world's folder), as before any update that moves data. 1.2.63 reads the store
   the earlier builds kept in the browser and never writes it.
2. **Optional:** in each GM's browser, with the world open, paste the line from
   the GM handbook, section 1, "Updating from a build before 1.2.63", into the
   console (F12). It saves every `danganronpa-rpg.` key of that browser to one
   file. That file holds every answer key the browser keeps, of every world it
   has opened: keep it where no player can open it.

## Changed

- **What only the GMs may know now lives in the GMs' browsers, one copy per
  world**: every Truth Bullet's answer key, every trace's real type and reading,
  who the Mastermind is and where the lair is, the running incident's cast and
  each chapter's Blackened, which planted object belongs to which trap and what
  waits in which room, the Observe declarations waiting for their roll, the
  Level Ups on offer, and which rooms each character has found. When a GM joins,
  the browsers exchange copies field by field and the newer decision wins, a
  removal included, so a GM who joins with an empty browser loses nothing and
  takes nothing away.
- **A player's browser holds only their part**: whether they are the Mastermind
  (and where the lair is when they are), the cast of an incident they are part
  of, the Level Ups offered to their own characters, and the rooms their
  characters have found. Players ask for it again when a GM's browser comes up,
  and are sent it again after a restore.
- **Back up the case and Restore the case** (GM panel, Between sessions) save
  the whole case to one file and merge it back. A restore takes only what is
  newer, shows what it would remove, and never takes the file's season reset.
  It takes another world's file, and that file's Mastermind or incident cast,
  only when you tick them. Keep the file where no player can open it.
- **When the primary GM's browser holds less than the world says it should** (a
  new browser, cleared site data), a health check names what is missing and
  offers Restore from a file, Enter the cast by hand for an incident in
  progress, or Move them into the ledger for old traces whose answer key is
  still on the token.
- **The season reset belongs to the primary GM**: another GM is told who that
  is, and the window names every GM who is not connected. A GM's browser that
  was away drops what the reset cleared the first time it opens the world. A
  reset that clears advancement withdraws the Level Ups on offer.
- **A Level Up on offer survives a change of primary GM.**
- **An Analyze of a Truth Bullet whose answer key is not on the GM's browser is
  refused**, instead of being scored Neutral, and gives back the action (or the
  Hope or Sanity) it cost. The GMs are told, once per bullet each session, that a
  backup can bring the key back. Handing such a bullet to someone else is
  refused the same way.
- **An Analyze or a handover of a Truth Bullet no longer waits without end when
  the GM's browser has not opened its answer keys**: after 16 seconds it is
  refused and paid back, the player is told why, and the GM is told once per
  session.
- **A GM's browser whose store of the case cannot open says so on screen**, not
  only in the console.
- **If a GM's browser cannot save the case** (its storage is full), the notice
  says whether another connected GM holds a copy, and asks for a backup.
- **A world updated straight from v1.1.0 keeps its safeword**; before, it was
  silently replaced by "Safe Word".
- **The regression suite waits for the world's load to finish writing** before
  it reads the world.

## Checked

- The headless suite: 360 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped, 0 red until a later stage. New in the
  suite: R169 to R189. New scenario 61-gmstore-case: GMs joining late, leaving
  and coming back, a restore, a reset and the players' copies, with 62 checks,
  all passing. The security scenario keeps its 71 checks; the other scenarios
  end as they did on 1.2.62.
- An independent review in two rounds, run while the stage was being written
  (round one: security, data safety, and whether the change is correct and its
  tests measure; round two: the same, in two parts), found two blockers, nine
  larger problems and thirty-two smaller ones, after removing those found twice.
  All are fixed here, each shown failing before it passed. The blockers: a
  player who had stopped being the Mastermind could keep the door and learn a
  new lair when two GMs' browsers disagreed, and an incident's cast claimed on
  the first load could take a third from an earlier incident and be sent to a
  player outside it. Among the larger ones: a restore of another world's file
  could remove this world's older rows on every GM, a trace's Faint Prep
  promotion could be lost on the first load, a GM with no cast in the browser
  could clear the cast by passing the turn, and the regression suite's fixtures
  could reach connected players' browsers.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks
  (LIVE-E04-01 to 12): the server's clock on v14, the size and time of the
  exchange between two GMs at a real table, the browser's storage after the
  update, a GM's network dropping and coming back, Back up and Restore in
  Chrome, Firefox and the desktop app, the update on a copy of a played world,
  two worlds in one browser, a murder finished after the GM changed browser,
  the reset refused to an Assistant GM, the safeword of a world from v1.1.0,
  two tabs of one browser, and the order in which a joining browser is seen.
  The local release gate needs a local Foundry v14 and did not run for this
  release.
